title_en: Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and Beijing Neiliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. — administrative dispute over trademark opposition review
ruling_gist_en: The applicant for the opposed trademark, as a competitor in the same region in the same trade, should have a considerable understanding of the fame and distinctiveness of the cited trademark. full_text_en:
Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and Beijing Neiliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. — administrative dispute concerning trademark opposition review

Ruling Summary

An applicant for an opposed trademark, being a competitor in the same industry and region, should reasonably have a certain degree of awareness of the reputation and distinctiveness of the cited trademark. Therefore, when registering and using a trademark on similar goods, the applicant for the opposed trademark shall observe the principle of good faith, pay attention to reasonable avoidance, and not maliciously exploit the reputation and goodwill of the cited trademark, so as to cause confusion or misidentification among the relevant public.

Although the opposed trademark may have objectively formed a certain market scale after being used for a certain period and scope, most of the use of the opposed trademark occurred after the filing date of the opposed trademark and before its approval for registration. Before extensively using the opposed trademark, the applicant should have recognized the legal risks that, due to the similarity between the opposed trademark and the cited trademark, and the high reputation and distinctiveness of the cited trademark, the opposed trademark might not be approved for registration, and the use of the opposed trademark might even infringe upon the registered trademark rights of the cited trademark. If the applicant fails to exercise reasonable duty of care and avoidance, and still applies for registration and extensively uses the opposed trademark, it shall bear the adverse consequences arising therefrom.

Supreme People's Court
Administrative Ruling

(2015) Zhi Xing Zi No. 116

Applicant for Retrial (Appellee at Second Instance, Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit 201, Building 3, Unit A, Longyuan Mansion, Miyun County, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Jingxin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Xinhua, Lawyer of Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Fan, Lawyer of Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce. Domicile: No. 1 Chama South Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: He Xunban, Director of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Sun Sha, Examiner of the Board.

Respondent (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Neiliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 34 Dazhalan Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Cheng Laixiang, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Shang Jiaquan, Lawyer of Beijing Gaowen Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fuliansheng Company), filed an application with this Court for retrial against the administrative judgment (2014) Gao Xing (Zhi) Zhong Zi No. 3252 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court on December 8, 2014, in a case concerning administrative dispute over trademark opposition review involving the respondents, the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board) and Beijing Neiliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Neiliansheng Company). This Court, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel to examine this case. The examination has now been concluded.

Fuliansheng Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: (1) The judgment of the second instance contains errors in fact-finding and application of law. First, the second instance judgment erred in finding that the opposed trademark and the cited trademark constitute similar trademarks. The opposed trademark is clearly different from the cited trademark in terms of constituent elements and overall appearance. The opposed trademark is a combination mark consisting of a graphic, the Chinese phonetic alphabet "FULIANSHENG", and the Chinese characters "福联升". Among them, the graphic is at the top with prominent visual effect and strong distinctiveness, while the Chinese characters "福联升" are at the bottom in artistic font. The cited trademark, on the other hand, is a pure word mark, with the characters "内联升" in calligraphic font, and the characters "联" and "升" are in traditional Chinese characters. The second instance judgment merely compared the character portions of the two trademarks, leading to a one-sided and erroneous conclusion. Second, for word marks, the first character often plays a major role in pronunciation, appearance, and meaning. If the first character or initial letter differs, they are usually not considered similar trademarks. In this case, the characters of the opposed trademark are "福联升", while those of the cited trademark are "内联升", with clear differences in pronunciation and meaning. According to established examination practice, the two trademarks should not be deemed similar. Third, the second instance judgment stated that "'联升' is not a fixed word combination but was originally created by Neiliansheng Company," which is inconsistent with the facts. Firstly, the word "联升" was not originally created by Beijing Neiliansheng Company. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing Dynasty, there was a person named "联升", whose birth and death dates are much earlier than the creation of "内联升". Secondly, there are numerous registrations of "联升" as a trademark or trade name across many goods or service categories and industries. Fourth, the second instance judgment failed to review the evidence submitted by the applicant for retrial during the review and litigation stages concerning the use and promotion of the opposed trademark, leading to erroneous conclusions. The applicant for retrial was established on September 13, 2006, and is mainly engaged in shoes, hats, clothing, bags, and other products. From the time of its establishment, the applicant began using "福联升" as its trade name and trademark, meaning "good fortune and promotion". Thereafter, it commissioned professionals to design its corporate visual identity system, hired the famous actress Niu Li as its brand image ambassador, and invested substantial advertising expenses to promote the old Beijing cloth shoe culture and establish a well-known brand with independent intellectual property rights. To date, the applicant has opened over 1,000 franchise stores in more than 30 provinces across the country, with products selling well nationwide and widely recognized by consumers. The second instance judgment, in determining whether the opposed trademark and the cited trademark are similar, did not review the evidence of use and promotion of the opposed trademark, thus reaching a one-sided and erroneous conclusion. (2) Through extensive and long-term use and promotion by the applicant for retrial, the opposed trademark has achieved relatively high reputation and has been widely accepted by consumers. Due to the significant differences between the applicant and the respondents in terms of trademark signs, storefront signage, store decoration, product categories, market positioning, and sales areas, the opposed trademark and the cited trademark have coexisted in the market without causing confusion or misidentification among the relevant public. The opposed trademark has been used for a long time, has established a high market reputation, and has formed a relevant consumer group. According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases on Trademark Authorization and Confirmation, the legislative spirit of balancing the protection of prior commercial mark rights and maintaining market order should be fully respected. The market reality where the relevant public has objectively differentiated the relevant commercial marks should be fully respected, and attention should be paid to maintaining the established and stable market order. The opposed trademark should be approved for registration. If it is not registered, it will cause substantial losses to the applicant for retrial and its franchisees, resulting in adverse social impact and being detrimental to social stability.

The Trademark Review Board submitted its defense opinion stating that it would comply with the judgment of the second instance.

Neiliansheng Company submitted its defense opinion as follows: (1) The opposed trademark and the cited trademark constitute similar trademarks on identical goods. Avoiding confusion as to source is the fundamental principle to be considered when determining trademark similarity, and the issue of similarity should be determined in light of the principle of good faith. Considering factors such as physical comparison, reputation, inherent distinctiveness, and the applicant's intention in choosing "联升", the two should be deemed similar. Specific reasons are as follows: First, the two trademarks differ only in the first characters "福" and "内". Second, regarding the inherent distinctiveness of "内联升", before the respondent used the words "联升", there was no evidence showing any connection or relationship between "联升" and "shoes" or "cloth shoes", and the applicant for retrial has not provided a reasonable explanation for using "福联升". Third, in terms of the difference in reputation between the two, the cited trademark is a well-known trademark in China, a time-honored brand, a national intangible cultural heritage, and has been awarded the title of "China's Number One Cloth Shoe House". It is well known by leaders of the Party and the state, celebrities, and the general public. In contrast, the applicant for retrial registered and used the opposed trademark for a relatively short time and lacks reputation. Fourth, "内联升" was approved for registration not merely because of its artistic font; therefore, the fact that the opposed trademark does not use the same artistic font as the cited trademark does not mean the two are not similar. The relevant public will not distinguish between the two trademarks based on the difference in font. In the market environment, the relevant public can easily be misled into believing that the cloth shoe products bearing the two trademarks originate from the same manufacturer or are related. Fifth, there is a likelihood of confusion or misidentification between the two trademarks. The two are similar in appearance, the goods are identical, the sales channels are the same, the consumer groups are the same, and the cited trademark has high inherent distinctiveness and reputation. Sixth, when examining the applicant's intention in using the word "联升", the following facts should be particularly noted: First, the applicant for retrial is a Shijiazhuang enterprise, actually producing and operating in Shijiazhuang, yet it registered "Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd." in Beijing and uses the words "Old Beijing Cloth Shoes" in its product advertising. Second, its registered trademark "福联祥" is composed of one character from each of two time-honored brands "内联升" and "瑞蚨祥", which constitutes a violation of good faith and an act of free-riding. Third, "福联升" is a combination of the respondent's cited trademark "内联升" and the trademark "福履" (No. 4730603), resulting in "福联升". Moreover, the applicant for retrial also combined the respondent's "内联升" with the time-honored brand and well-known trademark "瑞蚨祥" to register the trademark "祥联升" (No. 8467083), demonstrating a clear intention of unfair competition by exploiting goodwill. (2) The applicant for retrial violated the principle of good faith, infringing upon the respondent's prior trade name rights and prior trademark rights. First, before the opposed trademark was registered, the respondent's goods had acquired goodwill and reputation in the market and were known for certain distinctive features. Second, the applicant for retrial intentionally or unintentionally misrepresented a connection with the respondent, causing consumer confusion or misidentification. Third, the respondent has suffered or is likely to suffer damage, such as loss of customers, dilution of goodwill, or weakening of trademark distinctiveness. (3) The applicant for retrial has not used the opposed trademark for a long time. This is not a case of historical factors leading to coexistence of trademarks, but rather market coexistence resulting from unfair competition. Based on the protection of prior rights and consumer interests, the opposed trademark should not be approved for registration. (4) Any use that infringes upon prior lawful rights (or interests) cannot create any subsequent lawful rights. The applicant for retrial, ignoring the existence of the cited trademark, registered and used the opposed trademark on identical goods and cannot thereby obtain any lawful rights. The applicant for retrial should have recognized the potential infringement liability or inability to register the trademark if continuing to use trademarks related to "内联升" and should have ceased using the relevant trademarks. However, the applicant continued to register, use, and promote the relevant trademarks thereafter, and shall bear the consequences thereof. (5) "福联升" involves false advertising. Its claim that "福联升" was established in the spring of the 41st year of Qianlong's reign and was named by Ji Xiaolan, along with a fabricated story about Ji Xiaolan, easily misleads consumers into believing that the company is a time-honored brand with a long history, which is seriously inconsistent with the fact that it was established in 2006.

The applicant for retrial submitted six pieces of evidence to this Court, as follows: 1. Evidence 1, 2, and 6 are business licenses, contracts, and related photos of some of its franchise stores across the country, distributed in 28 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities, to prove that the opposed trademark has been used widely over a long period and has established a high market reputation. The photos of the franchise stores show signs bearing the words "Old Beijing Cloth Shoes" or "Beijing Cloth Shoes", "福联升", and the graphic part of the opposed trademark. The franchise contracts show that the signing places are all "Room 2305, Building C, Meidong International, Guang'an Street, Shijiazhuang City". The relevant contact numbers all start with 0311, but the address is "No. 168, Miyun Development Zone, Beijing". 2. Evidence 3 is a Baidu entry for "联升", to prove that there was a natural person named "联升" in the Qing Dynasty, and thus the word "联升" in the cited trademark is not original. 3. Evidence 4 is a search result of 143 trademarks containing "联升", to prove that "联升" is not original and is widely used across various goods and service categories. This evidence shows that, besides the opposed trademark, the applicant for retrial has applied for more than ten trademarks containing "联升" on shoes and other goods, such as "祥联升", "步联升", "鑫联升", "尚品福联升", "爱尚福联升", etc. 4. Evidence 5 is a detailed business search result, to prove that through business information inquiry, 55 enterprises (incomplete statistics) using "联升" as their trade name can be found. This Court will comment on whether the above evidence can achieve the applicant's purpose in the following paragraphs, in conjunction with the focus of this case.

This Court holds that the focus of this case is whether the opposed trademark and the cited trademark constitute similar trademarks, thereby violating Article 28 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2001) (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law).

Article 28 of the Trademark Law provides that where a trademark applied for registration is identical or similar to a trademark that has been registered by another person on the same or similar goods, it shall not be approved for registration. Regarding the determination of similarity of trademarks in civil disputes, Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks provides: "A people's court shall determine whether trademarks are identical or similar in accordance with the following principles: (1) based on the general attention of the relevant public; (2) both the overall comparison of the trademarks and the comparison of the main parts of the trademarks shall be conducted, and the comparison shall be carried out separately under the condition that the objects of comparison are isolated from each other; (3) when determining whether trademarks are similar, the distinctiveness and reputation of the registered trademark sought to be protected shall be considered." In accordance with Article 28 of the Trademark Law and with reference to the above judicial interpretation, this Court holds that the opposed trademark and the cited trademark are similar, violating Article 28 of the Trademark Law, for the following reasons.

First, from the perspective of pronunciation, appearance, and meaning of the two trademarks, although the opposed trademark contains both characters and a graphic, its character portion "福联升" is the phonetic part of the trademark and plays the main identifying role. Comparing "福联升" with the cited trademark, they differ only in the first character, while the remaining two characters "联升" are identical. The relevant public pronounces the two trademarks similarly. Moreover, the word "联升" in the cited trademark is not a fixed word combination. Although the applicant for retrial submitted Evidence 3 to show that there was a natural person named "联升" in the Qing Dynasty and that other trademarks or enterprise names also contain "联升", that person is not a well-known figure and is not familiar to the relevant public. The applicant also did not submit evidence to prove that before the filing date of the cited trademark, another person had used "联升" on shoes. Therefore, the second instance judgment's finding that "'联升' is not a fixed word combination but was originally created by Neiliansheng Company" is not improper.

Second, from the perspective of the distinctiveness and reputation of the cited trademark. According to the facts found in the first and second instance judgments and the examination by this Court, "内联升" is a well-known trademark in China, recognized as a time-honored brand, a national intangible cultural heritage, and awarded the title of "China's Number One Cloth Shoe House". Its cloth shoe products enjoy a very high reputation among the relevant public. Given such high distinctiveness and reputation of the cited trademark, the scope of trademarks considered similar to it should be broader than that of ordinary trademarks, and competitors in the same industry should correspondingly have a higher duty of attention and avoidance.

Third, regarding the reputation and use of the opposed trademark. The applicant for retrial submitted Evidence 1, 2, and 6 to prove that it has developed a number of franchise stores across 28 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities, achieving a certain degree of reputation. However, the said evidence can only prove that the opposed trademark was used in its franchise stores across various regions, forming a certain market scale, but is insufficient to prove that the opposed trademark has high reputation and distinctiveness. Given the high reputation and distinctiveness of the cited trademark and the similarity between the two trademark signs, the evidence submitted by the applicant for retrial is insufficient to prove that the opposed trademark and the cited trademark have formed an effective market distinction. When the relevant public applies ordinary attention, it is objectively still easy to cause confusion or misidentification as to the source of goods bearing the cited trademark and the opposed trademark, or to mistakenly believe that there is a specific connection between the goods designated by the opposed trademark and the cited trademark.

Finally, Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides: "Civil activities shall follow the principle of good faith." In this case, both the retrial applicant and the respondent manufacture and sell cloth shoes. As a competitor in the same region, the retrial applicant should have had a considerable degree of awareness of the respondent and its cited trademark's reputation and distinctiveness. Therefore, when registering and using trademarks on footwear, the retrial applicant should have complied with the principle of good faith, paid attention to reasonable avoidance rather than maliciously riding on the reputation and goodwill of the respondent and its cited trademark, thereby causing confusion among the relevant public. However, the evidence in this case indicates that the retrial applicant had obvious malicious intent to ride on the respondent and its cited trademark when registering and using the opposed trademark. First, the franchise agreements submitted by the retrial applicant all record the signing location as "Unit C, 23rd Floor, Meidong International, Guang'an Street, Shijiazhuang City," and the area code of the related contact telephone number is also 0311, indicating that its actual place of business is in Shijiazhuang, Hebei Province. However, the retrial applicant registered its enterprise in Miyun County, Beijing, and registered its enterprise name as "Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd.," which differs by only one character from the respondent's enterprise name. Thus, the retrial applicant intentionally aligned itself with the respondent and its cited trademark in terms of trademark, place of registration, and even enterprise name. Second, as previously stated, "Liansheng" in the cited trademark was first used by the respondent on cloth shoes and constitutes the main call and identifier of the cited trademark. The retrial applicant claims that its reason for using "Liansheng" is to convey the meaning of "joint development and rising." However, "joint development and rising" is neither a set phrase nor an existing term in the Chinese language, so the retrial applicant's stated reason for selecting "Liansheng" is clearly contrary to common sense. Third, the retrial applicant not only registered the opposed trademark containing the word "Liansheng" without justifiable reason, but also applied to register more than ten other trademarks containing "Liansheng" on similar and other categories of goods, further demonstrating its subjective malice. Fourth, although the opposed trademark has been used to a certain extent over time and has objectively formed a certain market scale, most of the use of the opposed trademark occurred after the filing date of the opposed trademark and before it was granted registration. Before extensively using the opposed trademark, the retrial applicant should have realized that because the opposed trademark is similar to the cited trademark, and the cited trademark has high reputation and distinctiveness, there was a legal risk that the opposed trademark would not be approved for registration and that the use of the opposed trademark could even infringe the registered trademark rights of the cited trademark. The retrial applicant failed to exercise reasonable care and avoidance, and still applied for registration and extensively used the opposed trademark. The adverse consequences arising from this should be borne by itself. On the contrary, in a situation where the retrial applicant, as a competitor, knew or should have known that the cited trademark has high reputation and distinctiveness, yet still maliciously applied for registration and used a similar opposed trademark, if the so-called market order or reputation formed by such conduct of the retrial applicant were still recognized, it would effectively encourage competitors to violate the principle of good faith, disregard others' legal prior rights, and forcibly build up and strengthen trademarks they have maliciously applied for. This would neither facilitate effective market differentiation nor help purify the environment for trademark registration and use, and would ultimately seriously harm the legal rights and interests of the prior trademark owner and the interests of the vast majority of consumers, violating the principle of good faith and the legislative purposes of the Trademark Law, including "protecting the exclusive right to use trademarks," "maintaining the reputation of trademarks," and "safeguarding the interests of consumers, producers, and operators." Therefore, the retrial applicant's claim that the opposed trademark, through use, has formed a certain market reputation and will not cause confusion among the relevant public lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the retrial application of Fuliansheng Company does not comply with the provisions of Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. This Court rules as follows:

The retrial application of Beijing Fuliansheng Shoes Co., Ltd. is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yanfang

Acting Judge: Du Weike

November 18, 2015
